title: Zoff Foods Pantry — A Seven-Point Spice Label Audit (2026)
description: What Zoff's own pages state about sourcing, cool grinding, batch codes and delivery — and a seven-point label audit you can run on any spice pack. Codes and single-origin claims not verified. Checked 26 Nov 2026.

forWho: Home cooks comparing whole spices, powders and blended masalas on label transparency rather than marketing words like 'clean' or 'pure'.
Shoppers who want a repeatable audit for any Indian spice pack, including Zoff's zip-lock formats.
skipIf: Anyone expecting a laboratory purity result from this page: Durza did not open, test or chemically analyse any Zoff pack.
Buyers who need a guaranteed working PANTRY20, ZOFF10 or prepaid stack — none was verified at checkout on 26 Nov 2026.
Anyone with spice or seed allergies, or who is buying for an infant or a medically restricted diet — check the exact ingredient list and ask a clinician.

content_blocks.heading: Are Zoff's spices 'clean label', and which claims can you actually verify?
content_blocks.body: Zoff's official story page states an own facility in Raipur, hand sorting, cool grinding below 60°C (it says a 40°C grinding cap elsewhere on the same page), zip-lock packs, batch codes and test-report-backed checks; the site banner says free delivery above ₹499. We did not open a batch report or a physical pack. The single-origin Guntur/Salem claim and PANTRY20/ZOFF10 codes in the older Durza draft were not found on the checked pages and are not claimed as active. Use the seven-point label audit below on the pack you receive.

items.title: What we could verify from Zoff's own site
items.body: The Our Story page says Zoff (Asquare Food and Beverages Pvt. Ltd.) operates its own Raipur facility, hand sorts and machine-cleans whole spices, uses an air-classifying mill for low-temperature grinding, packs in resealable zip-lock pouches, and states every pack carries a batch code. The site banner says free delivery above ₹499. These are brand statements about process, not purity results.

items.title: Cool grinding: note the two temperatures on one page
items.body: The same page says 'Cool ground below 60°C' and separately cites a '40°C Grind temperature cap'. Both are brand process claims. We did not see a temperature log or an independent audit, so this guide does not treat either number as verified.

items.title: Single origin: not verified
items.body: The older Durza draft asserted Guntur chilli and Salem turmeric as single-origin facts. The checked Zoff pages say raw material comes from India's main spice-growing regions and that sourcing information is available per product, but we did not find a pack-specific single-origin certificate. Do not repeat the claim as established.

items.title: Home adulteration tests are screening, not proof
items.body: Zoff's own blogs suggest checking FSSAI licence number, batch code, manufacturing date, and simple water/plate observations for turmeric. Such observations cannot confirm purity or rule out contamination; only a batch-linked laboratory report can. Zoff says test reports back its checks, but no report was opened for this guide.

items.title: Codes in the older draft were unverified
items.body: PANTRY20 (monthly masala boxes), ZOFF10 (sitewide) and a UPI prepaid stack were asserted in the static entry. None was visible or verified on the checked pages or in a cart on 26 Nov 2026. An email-gated FIRST25 first-order code appears on the site; we did not verify its terms at checkout.

items.body: Buy one or two packs first rather than a monthly bundle; check aroma, seal and label before committing to a subscription.

Run the seven-point label audit on arrival: FSSAI logo/licence, ingredient list, additives, batch/lot and dates, net quantity, brand/address, origin claim evidence, and any allergen/vegetarian declaration.
If a claim matters to you (single origin, no added salt, no preservatives), ask Zoff for the pack-specific statement or test report; the brand's page invites questions but Durza did not receive one.
Test any code in the cart. PANTRY20 and ZOFF10 were not verified on 26 Nov 2026; FIRST25 was visible but its terms were not checked. Do not count a saving until checkout accepts it.
Confirm final payable amount including delivery: the site banner says free delivery above ₹499, and delivery/discount terms are confirmed at checkout.

items.label: Zoff describes an own Raipur facility and batch codes
items.value: The official Our Story page states sourcing from India's main spice-growing regions, hand sorting, machine cleaning, air-classifying low-temperature grinding, resealable packs, batch codes and test-report-backed checks, with manufacturing at Urla, Raipur.

items.label: The page quotes two grind-temperature figures
items.value: Our Story states both 'Cool ground below 60°C' and a '40°C Grind temperature cap'. These are marketing/process claims; no temperature log or independent audit was provided or verified.

items.label: Zoff's own advice: check licence, batch and dates
items.value: Zoff's spice guidance blogs tell buyers to look for a valid FSSAI licence number, batch number, manufacturing date and sourcing information, and warn that unlabelled loose powder is unverifiable. Home water/plate tests are presented there as checks, not laboratory proof.

items.label: FSSAI requires core label declarations
items.value: The FSSAI (Labelling and Display) Regulations, 2020 require the food name, ingredient list, additive declarations, brand owner/importer details, FSSAI logo and licence number, quantity, date markings and related information on pre-packaged foods; a 2023 FSSAI FAQ notes the logo/licence must be in contrasting colour.

items.label: Single-origin claims need pack-level proof
items.value: Zoff's checked pages describe regional sourcing but no pack-specific Guntur/Salem single-origin certificate was found. Treat origin as a question for the brand, not a verified property of every pack.

items.label: Free delivery above ₹499 is stated on the site
items.value: The official site banner shown on 26 Nov 2026 says free delivery above ₹499; the cart itself says delivery, discounts and final availability are confirmed at checkout.

content_blocks.text: We checked Zoff Foods' Our Story page, two of its own spice-guidance blogs, and the FSSAI Labelling and Display framework (via the official compendium and an FAOLEX summary) on 26 Nov 2026. Brand process claims are reported as brand claims; we opened no pack, batch report or origin certificate, did not verify PANTRY20/ZOFF10/FIRST25 at checkout, and make no purity or health claim. Durza earns a commission on qualifying purchases through tracked links at no extra cost to you.

items: Original contribution — seven-point spice-label audit: (1) FSSAI logo + 14-digit licence visible and legible; (2) exact product name (whole, powder or blend); (3) ingredient list in descending order, with any salt or additive named; (4) batch/lot code plus manufacturing and best-before dates; (5) net quantity and MRP; (6) brand owner/manufacturer name and address; (7) any origin, 'no added salt/preservative' or purity claim backed by a pack-specific document. A clean-looking pack passes the audit; it is not a laboratory purity result.
The older Durza claims of single-origin Guntur chilli/Salem turmeric, no added salt/preservatives, prepaid stacking and the PANTRY20/ZOFF10 codes were not verified and are not asserted here.
Home water/plate tests for turmeric or chilli are screening observations only; a verified adulteration finding requires a laboratory report from the batch.

Stop using a spice and seek advice if it causes itching, swelling, breathing difficulty or severe GI symptoms; suspected deliberate adulteration should be reported to the retailer and FSSAI rather than self-tested further.
Spices are food ingredients, not medicines; this guide makes no antioxidant, immunity or disease-prevention claim.

items.a: We could not verify this. Zoff's checked pages say raw material comes from India's main spice-growing regions and that sourcing information is available, but no pack-specific Guntur/Salem origin certificate was located. The older Durza assertion is not repeated as fact.

items.q: Do the spices contain added salt or preservatives?
items.a: We did not open a pack or ingredient photograph, so we cannot confirm. Use the label audit: a single-ingredient powder should show only that spice; blends must list all ingredients and additives. Ask Zoff for the specific pack's declaration.

items.q: What does cool grinding below 60°C mean?
items.a: It is Zoff's stated process claim for protecting aroma oils. The same page also mentions a 40°C cap; no temperature log or independent audit was verified, so treat it as brand information, not a measured result.

items.q: Which code should I use — PANTRY20 or ZOFF10?
items.a: Neither is claimed as active. Both came from the older Durza draft and were not verified on 26 Nov 2026. A FIRST25 first-order code is shown on the site behind email signup, but its terms were not checked in a cart. Test any code at checkout and count only accepted savings.

No. Water-dispersion or plate tests can raise a question but cannot confirm purity or rule out contamination. Zoff's own blogs recommend checking FSSAI licence, batch and dates; a batch-linked laboratory report is the evidence that matters.
No. We compared public brand pages with the FSSAI labelling framework on 26 Nov 2026, opened no pack and commissioned no laboratory test. We make no purity or health claim.
